name: 06_template_anchor_label_collision
description: Stage 0 template match fires (keyword fingerprint matches this supplier's template). The template stores a short, generic anchor_label ('PO') for the variable po_number field — exactly the shape of anchor that pre-fix auto-generated templates persisted (see CLAUDE.md/perplexity notes on the 'PO' -> 'Polychemtex Inc.' collision), and that a user could plausibly still teach today for a supplier whose form genuinely just prints bare 'PO:'. The header text contains 'po' as a substring of two unrelated words ('Apollo', 'Components') BEFORE the genuine 'PO: 58820' line. The supplier's reference-number label ('PO:') is deliberately NOT one of the generic keyword_patterns labels (which all require 'No'/'Number'/'#'/'Ref' after 'PO'), so Stage 1 keyword matching also comes up empty for po_number — meaning the final result depends entirely on Stage 0's template anchor search, with no safety net. This is exactly the situation templates exist for (an unusual layout the generic patterns don't cover), and exactly the situation where a collision-prone anchor is most dangerous.
represents: The general anchor-label collision CLASS at the template-matching layer (Stage 0 / template_matcher.py::_find_by_anchor) — a sibling of the supplier-name substring-collision class covered by fixture 05, but in the text-anchor search rather than the hint-lookup. Any short, generic anchor fragment ('PO', 'Ref', 'No', 'Date', 'VAT') will keep colliding with ordinary words for any future supplier/template unless the search itself respects word boundaries.
